accepted_scope: Approves the release identities produced by this exact-SHA run: the 14-package inventory at the approved version with its SHA-256 manifest, and the container repository and immutable index digest covering exactly `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` with provenance mapped to the tested runtime SHA. Scope is limited to these artifact identities and does not itself authorize consumer migration.

limitations.rationale: Admission and write-fence interleavings are proven at the exercised live concurrency only; the consumer erasure and checkpoint-reset implementation is retained as the documented rollback.
Per-slot erasure is proven by the live-sidecar lane; completeness of the caller-owned slot inventory remains the caller's responsibility.
Authenticated stitched end-to-end erasure is evidenced through the live-sidecar path rather than a full authenticated UI traversal.
The global-administrator boundary is accepted as documented; erasure authority outside that boundary is unchanged by this closure.
Batch atomicity is bounded by the configured state store's transaction capability; non-transactional stores retain the consumer's coordinated detail/index write path.
ETag behaviour under batched writes is accepted as specified; callers continue to treat ETags as opaque validators.
Corrupt and abandoned envelope handling remains a retry and cleanup concern with the documented consumer rollback retained.
Terminal receipt retention is bounded by the configured retention policy rather than proven indefinite.
Cross-profile batching boundaries are unchanged by this evidence-only closure.
Preserve `Unknown` as a valid provenance outcome; handler-computed responses continue to resolve lifecycle evidence to `Unknown`.
All six operational values are preserved as the stable ABI.
The legacy query metadata ABI is preserved unchanged.
ETag never supplies lifecycle or version evidence; it remains an opaque validator per AD-15.
Legacy `/project` remains outside the v2 no-mixed-writer guarantee.
Mixed-writer protection covers exact named v2 routes only; the complete pre-cutover fleet and backup boundary are retained and no writer is rolled back across the global v2 marker.
Complete-prefix rebuild is bounded by the documented memory and byte limits.
The coordinated promotion boundary is accepted; page-only or incomplete staged output is never promoted.
Cancellation and resume semantics are accepted as documented.
Every deferred Story 1.19 review item remains owned and tracked in the deferred-work ledger.
Routine retained-key rotation is supported; key-ring loss or replacement remains a distinct documented recovery scenario, with opaque cursor handling and the consumer compatibility path preserved.
State writes made outside the projection handler contract remain the consumer's responsibility.
Stable work identity is accepted as specified for dispatch, retry, and ledger convergence.
Dead-letter and terminal cleanup behaviour is accepted as documented.
Null metadata behaviour is accepted as documented.
Versioned `/project/v2` is retained as the protected route.
Legacy `/project` is retained for compatibility and remains outside the v2 guarantee.
Exact `(Domain, ProjectionType)` routing identity is preserved.
The AD-19 bounded result contract is preserved.
The manifest-owned 14-package inventory and its byte identities are pinned by this run's SHA-256 manifest.
Container identity is pinned to the immutable index digest with exactly `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`, and provenance maps that digest to the tested runtime SHA.
Raw evidence is retained under an irreversible seven-year version-level WORM lock, bound by HTTPS URL and SHA-256.
Publication authority and the final migration decision are recorded in durable, role-bound GitHub records created before the operations they authorize.
